label: Mexico
goalHint: Finish first. The candidate with the most of the {total} presidency points wins outright: there is no second round and no share you must reach. National broadcasts reach the whole country, and regional pushes win the points a region holds.

issues.name: Crime and security
issues.blurb: Cartel violence, kidnappings, the army on the streets and who answers for the dead.

issues.name: Jobs and wages
issues.blurb: Wages, prices, informal work and whether the factories keep hiring.

issues.name: Corruption
issues.blurb: Governors who stole, contracts for friends and who goes to jail.

issues.name: Poverty and social programmes
issues.blurb: Cash transfers, pensions for the elderly and the forgotten south.

issues.name: Pemex and energy
issues.blurb: Oil, electricity and how much private money the state lets in.

issues.name: Democracy and the vote
issues.blurb: Clean elections, the electoral institute and the end of one-party rule.

issues.name: Trade, migration and the United States
issues.blurb: NAFTA, remittances, the border and the president in Washington.

regions.name: Nuevo León, Tamaulipas & San Luis Potosí

2000.label: 2000 · Fox v. Labastida
2000.tagline: July 2, 2000. The PRI has held the presidency for 71 years. Its candidate, Francisco Labastida, won the party's first open primary. Vicente Fox, the cowboy-booted former Coca-Cola executive, runs for the PAN and the Greens. Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas tries a third time for the left.

events.headline: Fox asks Cárdenas voters for a useful vote to end 71 years of PRI rule, and {party} gains among them
The first debate, April 25: Labastida complains on air that Fox has called him names, and the clip makes {party} look weak
Black Tuesday, May 23: the planned debate collapses over its format, Fox insists on 'today, today, today' in front of the cameras, and {party} looks stubborn
The second debate, May 26, comes three days after Black Tuesday and settles little. {party} keeps pressing its useful-vote appeal to Cárdenas voters
Porfirio Muñoz Ledo quits the race and backs Fox, and {party} picks up a voice from the left
Cárdenas fills the Zócalo to close his third run, and {party} holds its base in the capital and Michoacán
The PRI's governors turn out the old machine in the countryside, and {party} holds the rural vote
The Friends of Fox network raises money and volunteers outside the party, and {party} reaches voters the PAN never had
Labastida promises a new PRI, and voters who remember 1994 are not sure they believe it. {party} cannot escape its past

issues.name: Change
issues.blurb: Ending 71 years of PRI rule, in the first presidential vote run by a fully independent IFE.

issues.name: Economy and jobs
issues.blurb: Recovery from the 1994 peso crisis, wages that never caught up and Fox's pledge of 7 percent growth.

issues.name: Fobaproa and corruption
issues.blurb: The Fobaproa bank bailout that turned private debts into public ones, and graft under the PRI.

issues.name: Crime
issues.blurb: Kidnappings and street crime that had soared in Mexico City since the 1995 crisis.

issues.name: Poverty and Chiapas
issues.blurb: Progresa cash transfers, the poor south and Fox's promise to settle Chiapas in fifteen minutes.

issues.name: NAFTA and migration
issues.blurb: Six years of NAFTA, factory jobs on the border and migrants crossing north.

issues.name: Pemex and electricity
issues.blurb: Zedillo's failed 1999 bid to open electricity to private firms, and the future of Pemex.

2006.label: 2006 · Calderón v. López Obrador
2006.tagline: July 2, 2006. The former mayor of Mexico City, López Obrador, leads all winter for the PRD, the PT and Convergencia. The PAN's Felipe Calderón runs as the jobs president. The PRI's Roberto Madrazo, with the Greens, is fighting his own party. It ends 0.58 points apart.

events.headline: López Obrador opens the campaign ten points ahead, the mayor who survived the 2005 attempt to strip his immunity, and {party} looks unstoppable
López Obrador tells President Fox to shut up, 'cállate, chachalaca', and {party} hands its rivals the clip
PAN ads call López Obrador a danger to Mexico and compare him to Hugo Chávez, and {party} slips in the polls
López Obrador skips the first debate on April 25, and the empty chair costs {party}
At the second debate, June 6, López Obrador accuses Calderón's brother-in-law of profiting from government contracts, and {party} spends a week answering
Elba Esther Gordillo, the teachers' union leader, has broken with Madrazo, and {party} loses part of its machine on election day
Calderón promises to be the jobs president, with steady hands on the economy, and {party} owns the argument
Business groups pay for their own television ads warning against economic adventures, and {party} feels it
López Obrador points to the pensions for the elderly he paid as mayor, and {party} gains among older voters

issues.name: Jobs
issues.blurb: Calderón's pitch as the jobs president, slow growth and the millions who left to work in the US.

issues.name: Poverty and inequality
issues.blurb: López Obrador's 'for the good of all, the poor first', and his pensions for the elderly in Mexico City.

issues.name: Crime and kidnapping
issues.blurb: Kidnappings, the 2004 march against insecurity and drug violence in Michoacán and Nuevo Laredo.

issues.name: Corruption
issues.blurb: The PRD's 2004 video scandals, and the charges about Calderón's brother-in-law's contracts.

issues.name: Fox and fair play
issues.blurb: The 2005 attempt to strip López Obrador's immunity, and Fox's open campaigning for his party.

issues.name: Pemex
issues.blurb: Pemex's finances, and whether to let private investment into oil and electricity.

issues.name: Migration and the US
issues.blurb: The Sensenbrenner bill, the spring migrant marches in US cities and remittances sent home.

2012.label: 2012 · Peña Nieto v. López Obrador
2012.tagline: July 1, 2012. Twelve years after losing power the PRI is back with a young former governor of the State of Mexico and the Greens. López Obrador runs again for the PRD, the PT and Movimiento Ciudadano, promising a loving republic. Josefina Vázquez Mota is the PAN's first woman candidate, carrying Calderón's drug war.

events.headline: Peña Nieto opens the campaign far ahead, married to a television star and on every screen, and {party} plays it safe
Vázquez Mota's candidacy rally at the Estadio Azul ends with the stands emptying, and {party} looks adrift
The first debate, May 6: López Obrador goes after Peña Nieto and the PRI's return, the polls barely move, and {party} holds its base
May 11: students at the Ibero heckle Peña Nieto over the 2006 Atenco raid, #YoSoy132 is born, and {party} takes the hit
The Guardian publishes documents suggesting Televisa sold favourable coverage, and {party} spends the week denying it
The PRI's governors and the State of Mexico machine turn out the vote in the final week, and {party} holds its lead
López Obrador promises a loving republic and drops the anger of 2006, and {party} wins back some moderates
The toll of Calderón's drug war passes 50,000 dead, and the PAN's candidate wears it. {party} cannot change the subject

issues.name: Drug war
issues.blurb: Over 50,000 dead since Calderón sent the army against the cartels in December 2006.

issues.name: Jobs and wages
issues.blurb: The recovery after the 2009 crash, low wages and young people neither working nor studying.

issues.name: Corruption
issues.blurb: The PRI's former governors, from Coahuila's hidden debts to Tamaulipas, and the overruns on the Estela de Luz monument.

issues.name: Media and democracy
issues.blurb: #YoSoy132, claims that Televisa favoured Peña Nieto, and fears of the old PRI returning.

issues.name: Poverty
issues.blurb: Nearly half of Mexicans poor by CONEVAL's 2010 count, and the future of Oportunidades.

issues.name: Pemex
issues.blurb: Peña Nieto's call to let private investment into Pemex, against the left's defence of state oil.

2018.label: 2018 · López Obrador v. Anaya
2018.tagline: July 1, 2018. López Obrador's third run, now at the head of Morena, the party he founded, with the PT and the evangelical PES. Peña Nieto's government is sunk by scandal and the gasoline price rise, and its candidate Meade is not even a party member. The PAN's Ricardo Anaya leads a left and right alliance with the PRD.

events.headline: López Obrador opens his third run with a double-digit lead and a party of his own, and {party} looks hard to stop
Federal prosecutors look into a property sale linked to Anaya, and {party} spends weeks on money laundering questions
Meade cannot shake the Peña Nieto record: the White House mansion, Odebrecht and the gasoline price rise. {party} stays stuck in third
The second debate in Tijuana, May 20, on trade and Trump: Anaya attacks, López Obrador shrugs it off, and {party} keeps its lead
Business leaders warn against López Obrador's plan to cancel the new Mexico City airport, and {party} has to answer for it
The last debate in Mérida barely moves the polls, and {party} closes with a full Estadio Azteca
El Bronco proposes cutting off the hands of thieves at the first debate, and the night belongs to the front-runner
Anaya and Meade each ask the other's voters for a useful vote against López Obrador, and {party} pulls some over

issues.name: Corruption
issues.blurb: The 'White House' mansion, Odebrecht bribes and former governors like Javier Duarte in jail.

issues.name: Violence
issues.blurb: 2017, the most violent year on record, and the Internal Security Law keeping the army on the streets.

issues.name: Wages and growth
issues.blurb: Low wages, growth near 2 percent and the half-built new airport for Mexico City at Texcoco.

issues.name: Poverty and pensions
issues.blurb: López Obrador's promise of pensions for all the elderly and grants for the young, against targeted programmes.

issues.name: Trump and NAFTA
issues.blurb: Trump's border wall and the NAFTA renegotiation under way since 2017.

issues.name: Gasolinazo and oil
issues.blurb: The January 2017 fuel price rise, and whether to undo the 2013 opening of oil to private firms.

2024.label: 2024 · Sheinbaum v. Gálvez
2024.tagline: June 2, 2024. López Obrador cannot run again, his approval is near 60 percent, and his chosen successor carries Morena, the PT and the Greens. The PAN, the PRI and the PRD, old enemies, unite behind Xóchitl Gálvez. Movimiento Ciudadano runs alone and courts the young.

events.headline: Sheinbaum, López Obrador's chosen successor, opens the campaign with his approval near 60 percent, and {party} starts far ahead
Xóchitl Gálvez, the senator who sold gelatin as a girl, became the opposition's candidate after the president attacked her from his morning press conference. {party} has a story to tell
The first debate, April 7: Gálvez attacks, Sheinbaum stays calm, and {party} leaves with its lead intact

Gálvez opens her campaign at midnight in Fresnillo with families of victims of violence, and signs a pledge in her own blood in Irapuato not to abolish the social programs. {party} gets a crowd and a headline
A stage collapses in a gust of wind at a Movimiento Ciudadano rally in San Pedro Garza García on May 22, killing nine people. {party} suspends its campaign events
The pensions for the elderly reach every home in the final weeks, and {party} reminds each recipient who started them
Álvarez Máynez's jingle goes viral on TikTok, and {party} gains ground among young voters
Dozens of candidates for local office are murdered during the campaign, and the security record lands on {party}
Morena's ads call the alliance the PRIAN, the old parties back together, and {party} has to explain its partners

issues.name: Social programmes
issues.blurb: Pensions for everyone over 65, youth apprenticeships and grants, and whether a new government would keep them.

issues.name: Violence and security
issues.blurb: Some 30,000 murders a year, the 'hugs not bullets' policy and the National Guard under army command.

issues.name: Corruption
issues.blurb: Fraud at the Segalmex food agency, and the opposition parties' own records in government.

issues.name: Wages and nearshoring
issues.blurb: A minimum wage doubled since 2018, a strong peso and new factories moving to the north.

issues.name: Courts and the INE
issues.blurb: López Obrador's Plan C to elect judges by popular vote, and his clashes with the electoral institute.

issues.name: Health and medicines
issues.blurb: Medicine shortages after Seguro Popular was scrapped, and the IMSS-Bienestar system that replaced it.

issues.name: Pemex and energy
issues.blurb: Pemex's debts, the Dos Bocas refinery and state control of electricity.

events.headline: A fresh newspaper poll shows {party} gaining among undecided voters
A viral video, true or not, spreads faster than the campaign can answer, and {party} takes the hit
{party}'s candidate wins the debate, and the clip is on every network by morning
A popular governor lends {party} the state machine and his rallies for the final stretch
A massacre in a mid-sized city leads every newscast, and the governing side answers for it
The peso slides against the dollar, and the front-runner is asked what it means for prices
The electoral institute fines {party} for overspending, and the story runs for days
A packed rally in a central plaza electrifies {party}
{party}'s television spots land, and the jingle is on every radio
{party}'s caravan fills the plazas of three states in one weekend
The electoral authorities order one of {party}'s attack spots off the air
Business leaders warn about the front-runner's economic plans, and {party} spends the week answering
A former rival's local organisers switch to {party} in a televised ceremony
The electoral institute sets the next debate, and {party} must decide how to play it
events.prompt: The next debate is on every channel. How do you play it?

choices.text: Go on the attack against the front-runner
choices.resultText: You land blows and take a few. The overnight polls twitch your way.

choices.text: Play it safe and stay on message
choices.resultText: A steady night. No gaffes, no fireworks.

choices.text: Skip it: protect the lead and avoid the ambush
choices.resultText: The empty podium is the story of the night.

events.headline: Third-place voters are being asked for a useful vote, and {party} can make its own pitch
events.prompt: Supporters of the candidate in third could decide the race. What do you offer them?

choices.text: Ask them for a useful vote: a ballot for the third candidate is wasted
choices.resultText: Some come over. Their candidate's camp is furious.

choices.text: Adopt one of their signature pledges
choices.resultText: A few come over. Your own base wonders what changed.

choices.text: Ignore them and run to your own base
choices.resultText: Your base turns out. The third camp stays where it is.

events.headline: A small party offers {party} its registration and its slots on the ballot
events.prompt: The small party wants seats in Congress on your list and a ministry if you win. What do you do?

choices.text: Take the deal: their ballot line and their activists
choices.resultText: Their logo goes next to yours. The press counts what it cost.
Clean, and thinner on the ground.

choices.text: Refuse, and attack your rival's alliance of convenience
choices.resultText: You define them more than yourself, and it lands.
